card.name: Linking words before adverse reaction terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as to, for, of, because of and reported, right before a named side effect or symptom in adverse-reaction text. The next word is typically a symptom like somnolence, dizziness or joint pain.

modes.label: Reason for stopping
modes.description: A linking word after discontinued or because, leading into the side effect that caused it.
modes.example: About 3% of Levetiracetam-treated patients discontinued treatment due<< to>> somnolence, compared to

modes.label: Reported or cause of symptom
modes.description: A verb or preposition just before the symptom named in the sentence.
modes.example: 7% treated with placebo plus a stimulant<< reported>> somnolence. Before using ON

modes.label: Rate or cause of
modes.description: A word like for or of that leads into a symptom list.
modes.example: Consider DPP4 inhibitors as a possible cause<< for>> severe joint pain and discontinue drug if
